author: Michael Larabel
description: A patch that is queued up ahead of the Linux 7.5 merge window allows for optionally disabling /proc/kcore access at boot time. This can allow for better system security though will remain enabled by default for kernel builds with the typical CONFIG_PROC_KCORE option...
title: Linux 7.5 To Optionally Block /proc/kcore Access For Better Security

author: Michael Larabel
description: Back around 2017 an effort began to work on re-licensing all of the LLVM code under the Apache 2.0 license with exceptions, moving away from their prior 3-clause BSD-like "LLVM license". Prior updates on the topic included LLVM Developers Are Still Working On Their Massive Relicensing Effort (2018) and then LLVM Is Still Working On Relicensing, Needs Help Locating Some Past Contributors (2021)... Now finally as we approach the end of 2026, this re-licensing effort has been deemed effectively complete...
title: LLVM Effectively Completes Its Relicensing After Nearly A Decade Of Work

author: Michael Larabel
description: With recently having received a review sample of the GMKtec EVO-X2 mini PC powered by the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo" SoC and pre-loaded with Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, I took the opportunity to see how the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ performance is comparing between Windows 11 and Ubuntu 26.10 Linux on a range of workloads from gaming to AI and creator applications.
title: Windows 11 vs. Ubuntu 26.10 Linux Performance On AMD Ryzen AI Max+

author: Michael Larabel
description: After running weeks behind schedule due to PostgreSQL developers being overwhelmed by AI/LLM-led bug reports and security issues, PostgreSQL 19.0 managed to finally ship today...
title: PostgreSQL 19 Released With More Performance Improvements

author: Michael Larabel
